stops.name: Cologne, Therese and the sons take the house forward
stops.campa: With the founder gone, Therese Oppenheim takes up the direction of the house at the side of her sons Simon and Abraham. The widow whose signature already commands credit in many nations now governs a great bank: a woman at the head of Rhenish finance, unheard of in her time. Under her hand and her sons', the house will pour its capital into railways, mines, insurance and heavy industry, raising the Rhineland's machine age. From the Bonn ghetto to a two-century dynasty of Rhenish banking, the line holds. The founder's ledger of 1789 has become an inheritance; the house of Oppenheim enters the age its founder foresaw.
